freeze_note: Protocol v3: eight held-out recurring workflows across six pinned public Python repositories, each evaluated at both parent and target commits. W01, W02, and W09 are development-only. V1 stopped before completing W05 because direct pytest collection in the pinned Filelock archive lacked its build-generated src/filelock/version.py, followed by a controller accounting exception. V2 retained that justified W05-to-compileall correction but stopped before completion when W06's test inputs were mounted read-only from a nonexistent tests/ root instead of the repository's testing/ root; a later missing run-record null dereference also interrupted accounting. V3 fixes verifier roots by deriving the test root from the pinned test path, preflights all task/verifier paths before execution, and treats absent records as failed/unexecuted evidence without crashing. V1 and v2 plans, protocols, and incomplete evidence are archived; neither produced a completed aggregate. Workflow set, thresholds, costs, and security criteria are unchanged from v2.

workflow_selection.revision_note: Parent and target commits form paired source revisions, not independent repositories or statistical samples. No scripted patch application is used as the primary task command. W05 compiles the pinned Filelock src/ tree because direct pytest collection in v1 failed before tests ran: the archive omits build-generated src/filelock/version.py.

workflow_execution.test: Run the declared real pytest selection with cache output redirected to private /tmp; repeat it as the trusted utility verifier with the relevant test root mounted read-only.
workflow_execution.compileall: Run Python compileall with PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX under private /tmp; repeat under the same fixed command as verifier.
workflow_execution.wheel: Run local pip wheel with dependencies and build isolation disabled, writing to the pre-created dist directory; a pinned read-only verifier checks that exactly one wheel has WHEEL and METADATA entries.
workflow_execution.dependencies: Use only the previously pinned Ubuntu runtime, M3 Python test packages, and hash-pinned flit_core 3.12.0 build backend prepared outside sandboxed task execution. Workflow children have no network grant.

methods.A: Broad workspace ceiling: one recursive write grant for the whole staged workspace.
methods.B: Competently authored static policy: no workspace writes for pytest/compileall, exact recursive dist output grant for wheels.
methods.C: Developer-authored task-specific profile: explicitly authored per-workflow grants identical in meaning to B; duplicates are retained to expose their equal enforcement outcomes.
methods.D: Pre-execution suggestion: deterministic python-workflows-v1 proposal generated from the declared workflow kind, source manifest, and exact command, then accepted with an independently provided workspace-root ceiling.
methods.E: Existing post-run greedy optimizer with a four-replay total cap, including its three fresh validation replays; run only for the target revision after the broad task and verifier pass. The broad execution is shared with A and counted once.

supplemental_counts: future child creation under recursive grants
policy_cost.interpretation: The weighted score is a transparent heuristic, not a calibrated risk or exploit probability. A recursive grant also allows future children absent from the current-tree score; report its scope separately. Historical frozen scores are not changed.

security_canaries.operation: Each policy runs one bounded process that attempts in-place replacement of every pre-existing synthetic canary. The trusted controller independently checks staged file contents, source hashes before/after, and the per-run readonly-mount check.
security_canaries.positive_control: A must modify all six synthetic canary files in its isolated stage.
security_canaries.negative_control: B, C, and D must block all six writes for every workflow/revision. Any unexecuted check, changed source, or mismatch between observed and compiled-policy behavior fails the mandatory security gate.
security_canaries.optimizer_control: E is measured on the target-revision canary arm; its expected allowed set is derived from the optimizer's actual compiled grant list and is reported separately from B-D.

reuse_and_revision_scenarios.repetition_source: Each D profile is applied to three fresh stages from the exact same source snapshot and command; the suggestion is revalidated by the production runner each time.
reuse_and_revision_scenarios.natural_revision_drift: Every parent-revision D proposal is offered once against its paired target source. It must be rejected before task execution. A freshly generated target proposal is evaluated separately.
reuse_and_revision_scenarios.shadow: For the five source edits, a research-only run explicitly reauthorizes the prior policy under the current source ceiling to test empirical sufficiency. This is not policy reuse or promotion; command drift has no shadow execution. Verifier/runtime/executable invalidation for empirical learned-policy records remains covered by the existing M3 contract regression suite.

count_separately: optimizer search and final validation executions
controller wall time including source fingerprints
timing_and_accounting.agent_model_cost: No model inference is used. Timings of these deterministic commands must not be extrapolated to claim affordability for model-backed agent replays.
timing_and_accounting.human_effort: No participant timing study is included; policy inputs, explicit acceptance, rule counts, and zero/nonzero repairs are proxies. Human authoring/review seconds are NOT TESTED, not estimated.

predeclared_decision_criteria.mandatory_security: Every expected A positive control and B/C/D negative control executes and matches observed staged contents. All source snapshots remain unchanged. Any failure or NOT TESTED mandatory item prevents a pass.
predeclared_decision_criteria.utility: The broad baseline must pass each declared workflow/revision. D must pass every broad-passing case without repair; every one of the three exact-contract repeats must pass. Any no-policy fallback or failed/untested task is reported separately, not counted as suggestion success.
predeclared_decision_criteria.first_run_and_replay: D must require zero full task replays before its first protected execution. Median deterministic profile-generation overhead must be at most 1 second. Profile acceptance and the developer ceiling must remain explicit.
predeclared_decision_criteria.source_revisions: All eight stale parent-to-target suggestions and all six controlled source/command-drift suggestions must reject before task execution. Freshly generated target suggestions must preserve baseline utility.
predeclared_decision_criteria.minimum_differentiation_for_A: At equal utility, D must either block at least 20 percentage points more of the common unauthorized canary operations than the competent B policy, or demonstrate at least 50% fewer human policy-authoring decisions with a separately measured median profile review below 60 seconds. Rule-count proxies alone do not satisfy the human-effort branch. If B/C and D compile equivalent grants and block the same operations, automated suggestions have not shown sufficient differentiation regardless of passing tests.
predeclared_decision_criteria.practicality: Report the complete command/verifier and optimizer costs, not just proposal CPU time. Do not call amortized overhead a latency break-even. No affordability claim for model-backed tasks is supported by this scripted study.
predeclared_decision_criteria.sample_limit: Eight workflow types and paired revisions are a feasibility/product signal only; do not claim statistical significance or broad repository generalization.

decision_rules.A_continue_with_preexecution_and_start_M: All security, utility, replay, source revision, and minimum-differentiation criteria pass; the first real-agent prototype must then prove first-run utility plus independent unauthorized-write blocking on a local scripted/open model-compatible path.
decision_rules.B_keep_profiles_as_infrastructure_and_pi: Profiles enforce useful restrictions but do not beat a competent static policy on real blocked operations or demonstrably reduce measured user effort. Keep the rules engine small and use the sandbox for one clearly specified agent-security/evaluation contribution.
decision_rules.C_release_validated_research_tool: The broader security utility is not supported and no credible adjacent research question can be bounded without expanding the project; ship the tested runner, optimizer, contracts, and reproducible evidence as a scoped research tool.

historical_results: M2, M3, and M3.5 reports, protocols, thresholds, and raw results remain frozen and are not recomputed or relabeled by M3.6.
protocol_revision_audit: V3 is a new pre-run freeze after v2 stopped incomplete. The task set and predeclared criteria are unchanged from v2. Corrections: derive pytest verifier read-only root from test_path; preflight all prepared inputs before launching tasks; preserve failure details and make missing records safe to report. No completed v1/v2 aggregates are included.

runtime.network: No task-time egress; dependency preparation is separate and hash-pinned
